Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the Nexara Cloud Technologies Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing Nexara Cloud Technologies's results for the Q3 2024. With me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Morgan Patel, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Nexara Cloud had an exceptional Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas: expanding our market share in key verticals, investing in cutting-edge research and development, enhancing our cloud security posture, driving operational efficiencies, and strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

I'm thrilled with our performance across the board, but today I want to zoom in on one of the most transformative drivers of our business: the explosive growth in AI and machine learning workloads. As the leading hyperscaler in enterprise-grade cloud infrastructure—right there with AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud—we've seen AI/ML adoption skyrocket, fueled by the generative AI revolution that started with models like GPT-4 and Stable Diffusion last year. Let me share the data, trends, and strategic moves that position us for sustained leadership.

First, the headline numbers. In Q3, AI/ML workloads—which we define as compute-intensive tasks including training, fine-tuning, inference, and retrieval-augmented generation pipelines—grew 48% year-over-year and 22% quarter-over-quarter. This outpaced our overall cloud revenue growth of 31% YoY, now representing 28% of our total remaining performance obligations, up from 19% a year ago. Our AI/ML annual recurring revenue hit $4.2 billion, a 52% YoY increase, driven by an average customer spend on AI services jumping 35% to $1.8 million per enterprise account. That's comparable to what early adopters saw with SageMaker on AWS or Vertex AI on GCP during their inflection points, but we're accelerating faster thanks to our hybrid edge-cloud architecture.

Adoption rates tell an even more compelling story. Over 72% of our top 1,000 customers—Fortune 500 names in financial services, healthcare, and autonomous systems like major banks and pharma giants—are now running production AI/ML workloads on our platform, up from 55% last quarter. Self-serve adoption via our Nexara ML Studio is booming: developer sign-ups for free-tier GPU instances surged 180% YoY, converting to paid workloads at a 65% rate within 90 days. We're seeing this across verticals—retail customers using our platform for personalized recommendation engines report 40% uplift in conversion rates, while manufacturing firms are deploying predictive maintenance models that cut downtime by 25%.

The shift from training to inference is massive: inference workloads, which are real-time and latency-sensitive, now account for 62% of AI/ML compute hours, up from 45% last year. This mirrors industry-wide patterns post-Llama 2 and Mistral releases, where enterprises prioritize scalable serving over one-off training. We're also witnessing multimodal AI takeoff—combining vision, language, and audio—with workloads for models like our open-source Nexara-Vision-LLM growing 110% quarter-over-quarter. Cost pressures are real amid NVIDIA H100 shortages; our customers are optimizing with model pruning and quantization, achieving 3-5x inference efficiency gains on our platform. Sustainability matters too—our AI workloads run on 100% carbon-neutral data centers, with PUE averaging 1.15, helping clients meet ESG mandates that others are still addressing.

On the technical front, our initiatives are purpose-built for this surge. We've doubled down on custom silicon: our Nexara Trainium2 accelerators, now generally available, deliver 4x the training throughput of off-the-shelf A100s at 60% lower cost per FLOP, powering 40% of large-scale training jobs. For inference, Inferentia3 chips handle 10 million tokens per second for Llama 3-scale models, with autoscaling fleets that ramp from zero to 1,000 GPUs in under 60 seconds. We've integrated these with our Astra ML Platform, offering end-to-end MLOps—from AutoML for no-code fine-tuning to Kubeflow-compatible pipelines. Key partnerships amplify this: our NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD collaboration provides H200 access for the biggest jobs, while Habana Gaudi3 integration caters to price-sensitive hyperscale training. Our open-source contributions to Hugging Face Transformers and ONNX Runtime have driven 25% more ecosystem traffic to our inference endpoints.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, with AI/ML growth at 55% YoY, led by Silicon Valley tech firms and Wall Street quants building fraud detection systems. EMEA is accelerating at 42% YoY, boosted by GDPR-compliant sovereign clouds in Germany and France; we're capturing share from Azure with FedRAMP High and EU Data Boundary certifications. APAC is at 38% YoY growth, dominated by Japan and India, where enterprises are scaling agentic AI for robotics. China exposure is limited to 5% of AI ARR due to regulations, but partnerships with Alibaba Cloud for cross-border hybrid setups are yielding 20% month-over-month upticks in inference traffic. LatAm and MEA are nascent but promising, with 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in Brazil's fintech scene adopting our cost-optimized TPU alternatives.

Strategically, we're shaping the wave. We've committed $5 billion in CapEx for FY24 to expand AI-optimized capacity by 3x, including new zones in Tokyo, Sydney, and São Paulo. Our Nexara AI Marketplace now hosts 1,200 pre-trained models, with serverless deployment slashing time-to-value by 70%. To combat commoditization from open models like Grok or Phi-3, we're investing in proprietary vertical AI: Nexara BioForge for drug discovery and Nexara FinML for real-time risk modeling. Customer lock-in is strong—multi-year commitments for reserved AI instances now represent 45% of new ACV, with net revenue retention at 128%. Risks include GPU supply chain volatility and regulatory scrutiny on energy use, but our diversified silicon stack and green commitments mitigate that.

Looking ahead, we guide AI/ML workloads to grow 45-50% YoY in FY25, pushing total cloud revenue toward $28 billion. This is the structural shift to AI-native clouds, where Nexara's full-stack leadership gives us durable moats.

Now I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in the Q3. Revenue grew by 31% year-over-year to $28 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 71.2%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 32%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our Cloud Services segment gross margin, which came in at 71.2% for the quarter—up 320 basis points year-over-year and 110 basis points quarter-over-quarter. This marks our 12th consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion in Cloud Services, reflecting the structural profitability levers we've been pulling as we scale to over $28 billion in quarterly revenue. For context, this outperforms the hyperscaler peer set, where AWS reported 69% in their last quarter, Azure hovered around 70%, and Google Cloud continues its catch-up at 62%, still grappling with heavier infrastructure investments.

Let me break down the key factors influencing this profitability, starting with the headline drivers, then regional nuances, technical initiatives, and our strategic outlook.

The biggest tailwind remains our ongoing shift toward higher-margin services. IaaS compute and storage, which carry margins in the mid-60s, now represent just 42% of Cloud Services revenue, down from 48% a year ago. In contrast, PaaS and SaaS offerings—like our Nexara AI Studio, serverless compute, and managed Kubernetes—have grown to 35% of the mix, delivering margins above 80%.

AI and machine learning workloads were the star here: AI-related revenue surged 145% YoY to $4.2 billion, fueled by demand for our custom TPUs and GPU clusters optimized for large language models. These services boast gross margins north of 85%, thanks to software-defined efficiencies and lower incremental hardware costs per inference. We've seen similar dynamics at peers. Without this mix shift, our headline margin would have been closer to 69.5%.

Utilization across our 45 global hyperscale data centers hit a record 85%, up from 79% YoY, directly leveraging our $18 billion in FY24 capex. This scale is compressing unit costs: average revenue per rack jumped 22% to $1.2 million annualized, while cost per rack fell 8% to $340k, driven by denser packing of NVIDIA H100s and our in-house Nexara Graviton4 Arm-based chips, which deliver 40% better price-performance than x86 alternatives.

Depreciation and amortization as a percentage of revenue improved to 18.2% from 20.1% YoY, as we've lapped heavier buildouts from the post-pandemic boom. Power costs, a whopping 25% of COGS, benefited from our PUE averaging 1.15—best-in-class—through liquid cooling retrofits and demand-response programs with utilities.

We've aggressively optimized the cost stack. Bandwidth costs dropped 12% YoY via our private fiber backbone expansion, now spanning 1.2 million km and peering directly with Tier 1 ISPs. Renewable energy sourcing hit 65% of our footprint, up from 52%, hedging against rising electricity prices amid data center power crunches in Virginia and Ireland.

Software efficiencies are key: Our orchestration layer reduced idle compute by 28% through predictive autoscaling. We also passed through 3-5% list price increases on legacy instances in June, capturing pricing power as customers lock in via 3-year Reserved Instances, which now represent 62% of compute spend.

Offsetting pressures included a 50bps forex headwind from a stronger USD versus the euro and yen, and $150 million in one-time hyperscaler chip qualification costs for next-gen Blackwell GPUs. Competitive pricing in storage remained intense, with object storage margins at 68% amid pressure from low-cost providers.

Regionally: North America, 55% of revenue, margins at 73.5%, buoyed by mature utilization and AI demand from big tech. EMEA, 22%, 70.1% margins, up 400bps YoY, optimized post-Brexit, though energy costs in Ireland remain elevated. APAC, 18%, lagging at 67.8% from buildouts, but growth explosive at 42% YoY—margins to inflect to 70%+ by Q1'25. Latin America & Other, 5%, 66.2%, pressured by currency and investments, offset by public sector wins.

Looking ahead, we're doubling down: Graviton5 enters production Q4, targeting 25% cost savings; $2 billion in inference-as-a-service; edge computing margins at 82%; net-zero by 2035 with SMR deals. Open-sourcing container runtime boosts SaaS margins.

We expect Cloud Services gross margin to expand another 200bps to 73-74% in Q4, full-year FY24 at 70.5%. Our $120 billion RPO, up 33% YoY, provides visibility. As AI capex peaks, we'll pivot to opex-light services, targeting 75%+ by FY26.

Now, I'll hand it over to Taylor Kim for a technical update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new ForgeAI platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm thrilled to dive into our new service launches and the phenomenal market reception they've received this quarter. The cloud computing landscape is evolving rapidly, driven by generative AI workloads, edge computing for low-latency apps, and sovereign cloud solutions amid data privacy regulations. We've leaned into these with three major launches in Q3, contributing $450 million in initial bookings—18% of quarterly revenue—and on track for over 25% YoY growth in PaaS and SaaS by FY24 end.

First, ForgeAI Ultra, our fully managed generative AI platform launched August 15th. It integrates fine-tuned foundation models from partners like Anthropic and Stability AI, with native NVIDIA H100 support and proprietary auto-scaling serverless inference. Optimized for enterprise RAG, it reduces latency 40% vs. AWS Bedrock or Azure OpenAI, cutting TCO 35% via predictive orchestration. Reception outstanding: 1,200 enterprise customers in 45 days, including top automakers migrating 50 PB data and health firms for HIPAA-compliant pipelines. Early ARR $120 million, net retention 142%. Gartner and Forrester position us with Vertex AI.

Next, EdgeForge Network, distributed edge computing rolled out September 1st. 100+ global PoPs with sub-10ms latency, integrated with ForgeKube 2.0 Kubernetes and zero-trust enclaves. Addresses hybrid needs—68% of enterprises per our survey. 850 sign-ups, $180 million RPO, 65% greenfield. Partnership with major telcos for 5G slicing across Europe, 28% faster processing. In APAC, 22% market share among telcos.

Finally, SovereignShield, compliant sovereign cloud launched October 1st. Air-gapped zones with FIPS 140-3 and compliance for GDPR, FedRAMP, IRAP. Counters sovereignty push—420 customers, $150 million bookings, NPS 78, churn under 2%.

Regionally: Americas 52% of bookings, 32% AI growth; EMEA 41%, SovereignShield key; APAC 55%, EdgeForge; LATAM 22%.

These underscore our AI Everywhere thesis: $2.8 billion R&D blending IaaS/PaaS, open APIs for Kubernetes. Sustainability—27% carbon reduction. Expect $1.2 billion FY24 ARR, 72% margins, 1.5 points market share gain.

I'll now pass it to Morgan Patel for a product roadmap update.

Morgan Patel:
Thank you, Taylor. This quarter, we launched Nexara Savings Plans enhancements, game-changing for enterprise optimization. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into the impact of our pricing strategies and discounting programs. In this hyper-competitive landscape—head-to-head with AWS, Azure, GCP—pricing is a strategic weapon for acquisition, retention, expansion, and margins. We've balanced aggressive discounting with premium pricing to deliver 28% revenue growth to $22.4 billion FY, expanding operating margins to 32.1%.

Our portfolio: pay-as-you-go on-demand ($0.10-$0.25/vCPU-hour); Reserved Instances 40-75% off; Savings Plans up to 66%; Spot 70-90% for interruptible; CUDs for sovereign.

Revenue impact: 15% workload consumption increase despite 24% average discount (up from 21%). Net pricing expansion 8% from mix—AI Accelerators to 18% revenue, 15-20% premiums. Startup Credits ramp cohorts 35% higher spend; top enterprises 55% Savings penetration, 2.5x growth.

Margins: Discounting compressed gross 180bps to 74.2%, offset by FinOps—Cost Optimizer cuts waste 28%. PaaS attach 62%. VolumeFlex incentives lift bundling.

Regional: NA 18% discounts, 32% growth; EMEA 28%, 41% growth; APAC 32%, 55% growth; LatAm 25%, 62% growth.

Forward: Dynamic Savings Plans 2.0 AI-optimized; premium tiers for GenAI. Risks competition, but 85% retention, 40% expansion resilient. Smart discounting accelerates.

Now, back to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Morgan. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Before diving deeper, I want to unpack the impact of foreign exchange fluctuations on our reported revenue, key for constant currency view. With over 65% of $28 billion Q3 revenue international, we're exposed like peers. Strengthening USD created headwind, but hedging mitigated.

Reported revenue 31% YoY to $28 billion; constant currency 34%, FX shaved 300bps or $85 million headwind, up from Q1's $45 million.

Regional: EMEA 32% revenue, euro -7%, GBP -5%, $42 million hit—offset by sovereign clouds. APAC 25%, yen -9% $28 million, but India strong. Rest 8%, $8 million.

Trailing 12-month constant currency 34% vs. 31% reported; RPO $120 billion up 33% constant.

Mitigations: 70-80% hedged, $55 million gains; 60% local costs; localized pricing 40% top customers; usage-based elasticity; sovereign builds like Saudi.

Q3 guide reflects 1-2% headwind; long-term global footprint outperforms.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Ben Smith:
Thanks for taking my question. Jordan, great detail on the gross margins—impressive expansion. Can you expand on the APAC dynamics and when we should see that inflect?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Ben. Happy to address. In APAC, margins at 67.8% reflect aggressive buildout—$4.5 billion YTD capex in Singapore and Tokyo pushing D&A higher. But growth is 42% YoY from GenAI demand by telcos and enterprises migrating on-prem. Utilization will ramp, inflecting to 70%+ by Q1'25 as Graviton chips and AI infra come online. We're confident.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, thanks. Morgan, on pricing, with discounts up to 32% in APAC, how are you balancing competitiveness and margins long-term?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Lisa. We're shifting to usage-based incentives like VolumeFlex and Dynamic Savings Plans 2.0, which encourage bundling and right-sizing—PaaS attach now 62%. In APAC, Flex Pricing blends Spot savings with SLAs. This recaptures via velocity—$4.8 billion discount recapture FY—and high-margin AI premiums protect blends. Resilient at 72%+ coverage target.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Taylor, the new launches sound strong—ForgeAI Ultra adoption metrics and competitive positioning?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Raj. ForgeAI Ultra's 1,200 customers and $120 million ARR in 45 days, with 142% NRR, validate. 40% lower latency, 35% TCO vs. Bedrock/Vertex, Gartner peers us equally. Integrates our Trainium/Inferentia for efficiency. EdgeForge and SovereignShield similarly stellar—positioning us for multi-cloud leadership.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in Nexara Cloud Technologies. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
